principles: PostgreSQL remains authoritative for transactional business state.
A capability stays in PostgreSQL when relational consistency and unified queries outweigh resource and lifecycle cost.
Every derived copy names its authority, freshness, idempotency, reconciliation, rebuild, failure, deletion, and exit behavior.
Extensions are admitted by service tier and lifecycle state, not merely by installability.
No proposal target is reported as an achieved SLO before lower-volume validation.
The platform reference implementation can change without changing the capability contract.

capability_decisions.consistency: constraints and transactions define order, inventory, and payment invariants
short invariant enforcement may use constraints, functions, and triggers
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: long-running orchestration, remote calls, or unbounded retry moves to an external worker

capability_decisions.consistency: searchable projection is transactionally maintained with product state
evidence: ch15 exact golden and ranked quality evidence
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: quality, scale, language, or independent availability SLO fails the PostgreSQL baseline

capability_decisions.consistency: embedding model identity and vector dimension are versioned
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: ANN scale, quality, rebuild, or independent service SLO fails the production benchmark

capability_decisions.consistency: UTC event time, versioned validity, EPSG:4326 identity, and boundary policy are contractual
capability_decisions.freshness: event ingest plus explicitly measured lateness
evidence: ch16 frozen time, space, boundary, and partition evidence
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: retention, compression, routing, or analytical throughput misses measured service objectives

capability_decisions.consistency: reports name their source watermark and freshness
capability_decisions.freshness: offline replica or summary lag is explicit
evidence: ch17 parallel, covering-index, spill, and summary evidence
ch17 naive versus two-stage FDW transfer shape
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: representative capacity evidence crosses a single-node or offline-replica boundary

capability_decisions.consistency: cache version never supersedes newer PostgreSQL product state
evidence: contract-only; no external cache L1 has been run
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: measured read amplification or latency justifies a cache

capability_decisions.consistency: business change and publication intent commit atomically; delivery is at-least-once
evidence: contract-only; no event-bus L1 has been run
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: another service needs durable asynchronous delivery or replay

capability_decisions.consistency: object bytes and PostgreSQL metadata agree by immutable identity and checksum
capability_decisions.freshness: visible only after upload and metadata finalization
evidence: architecture contract; L1 object workflow is pending
capability_decisions.externalization_trigger: always external for authoritative media bytes

logical_nodes.purpose: HA candidates and reviewed read-only traffic
OLAP, ETL, and interactive slow reads with explicit lag

topology.failure_domains: must be proven in chapter 19 rather than inferred from node count
topology.distributed_sharding: deferred; Citus requires a new ADR after chapter 26 evidence

security.external_secrets: not stored in this repository blueprint
security.tenant_isolation: must be selected and proven in chapter 23

service_signals: CPU, memory, storage, temp, WAL, and replication lag

exit_paths: Every derived cache, search, or analytical projection can be rebuilt from its named authority.
Extension-owned data has a portable export and restore path before production admission.
Service routing can return to PostgreSQL-only behavior while external consumers drain.
A Citus or specialized analytical adoption requires a separate reverse-migration rehearsal.
Database and object-storage authority are reconciled by stable identity and checksum before provider migration.
limitations: This blueprint validates document relationships and current development fixtures; it does not deploy production infrastructure.
All service objectives remain proposals until the lower-volume chapters produce evidence.
The local database contains teaching schemas that are not all intended for one production cluster.
The loopback postgres_fdw lab and password_required=false are explicitly excluded from production admission.
Product names for cache, message bus, object storage, search, and lakehouse are deliberately undecided.
Citus and specialized OLAP remain conditional alternatives, not selected production components.
